question: Should explicit requester consumption be accepted as durable delivery proof for a descendant even when a later outward send from that requester fails?
rationale: The code deliberately changes the meaning of delivered state and therefore suppresses existing retry/finalization behavior; tests can verify mechanics but cannot choose the product-level delivery contract.

options.title: Require proof and semantic sign-off
options.body: Require redacted cron/background or SQLite restore evidence and confirm that requester consumption is the intended delivered boundary before merge.

options.title: Preserve retry until outward delivery
options.body: Keep descendants retryable until the requester’s final outward delivery succeeds, which requires a different state model than this PR.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox work
options.body: Pause this focused change and resolve the contract through the broader durable completion-inbox work tracked by the related delivery issue.

recommendation.title: Require proof and semantic sign-off
recommendation.body: Require redacted cron/background or SQLite restore evidence and confirm that requester consumption is the intended delivered boundary before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged announce-delivery work is the closest identified current-main history for the delivery-boundary decision.
